extracted.intended_audience: public relations counselors, corporate executives, and students of public relations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for the work and responsibilities of a public relations counsel: how to study public opinion, design campaigns, choose media, advise clients on policy and conduct, and act ethically to shape public judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide when to use or omit competitor prices in advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: A client is advised to use prices in its advertising, another store not to mention them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess context and competitive dynamics before publishing prices; some situations benefit from transparent price advertising, others from omission to avoid direct price comparison or legal/competitive pitfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage client labor policy and hygienic practices as PR assets
rubrics_metrics.description: A client is advised to make his labor policy, the hygienic aspect of his factory, his own personality, part of his sales campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate internal policies (working conditions, hygiene, leadership persona) into external messaging to build trust and differentiate the product beyond technical qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use educational and cultural venues to exhibit wares
rubrics_metrics.description: Another client is advised to exhibit his wares in a museum and school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place products in scholarly or cultural settings to confer legitimacy and reach influential audiences; adapt presentation to the institution's tone and audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ philanthropy and scholarships as long-term PR strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Still another is urged to found a scholarship in his subject at a leading university.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use charitable endowments and academic support to create durable goodwill and association with expertise; ensure authenticity and alignment with corporate values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create circumstances and events to attract favorable attention
rubrics_metrics.description: There are the circumstances and events he helps to create. After that there are the instruments by which he broadcasts facts and ideas to the public...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan and stage events, productions, exhibitions or newsworthy actions that generate storylines and public engagement rather than rely on chance publicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act as counsel rather than mere 'publicity man'
rubrics_metrics.description: A man who is really counsel or director of public relations has one of the most important jobs... a man who merely represents the old idea of getting something for nothing from publishers is about passé.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize strategic advice, policy shaping, and long-term reputation management over quick stunts or one-off publisher favors; maintain professional standards and responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize the public's demand for information and judgment role
rubrics_metrics.description: The public to-day demands information and expects also to be accepted as judge and jury in matters that have a wide public import.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accurate, timely information and accept that the public will evaluate actions; transparency and responsiveness are necessary to maintain credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for organizations' semi-public status
rubrics_metrics.description: The tendency of small organizations to aggregate into groups of such size and importance that the public tends to regard them as semi-public services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat large private firms and associations with the attentiveness of public institutions—anticipate scrutiny and obligations that flow from perceived public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to increased public willingness to be heard
rubrics_metrics.description: The increased readiness of the public, due to the spread of literacy and democratic forms of government, to feel that it is entitled to its voice in the conduct of these large aggregations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design channels for feedback and participation; expect and facilitate public input into corporate and organizational decisions when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for keen competition for public favor
rubrics_metrics.description: The keen competition for public favor due to modern methods of 'selling.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate messaging, broaden appeal beyond product features, and integrate reputation-building activities to compete effectively for attention and preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use informative publicity to stabilize markets and perceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Really informative publicity 'would protect the great majority of operators from the criticism that can only be properly leveled at the minority.' (Hoover on coal example)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide industry-wide facts and context to educate consumers and stakeholders, which can reduce rumor, speculation, and undue criticism; aim for informative campaigns that raise understanding of supply, demand and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-way interpretation: interpret organization to public and public to organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Some public utilities maintain public relations departments, whose function it is to interpret the organizations to the public, as much as to interpret the public to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build mechanisms for both outward communication and inward listening; PR should translate institutional realities for the public and convey public sentiment back to leadership for decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperate with community movements and civic organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: It coöperates, for example, with such movements as the Welcome Stranger Committee of New York City... It coöperates with conventions, to the extent of arranging special travel facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage in partnerships, sponsorships, and cooperative programs that deliver public value and showcase organizational service; tailor contributions to community needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain continuous PR efforts even for non-competitive services
rubrics_metrics.description: Even a service which is in a large measure non-competitive must continually 'sell' itself to the public, as evidenced by the strenuous efforts of the New York subways and elevated lines to keep themselves constantly before the people in the most favorable possible aspect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustain ongoing visibility and messaging to manage expectations, cultivate patience for unavoidable inconveniences, and highlight constructive improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use publicity for public education in health and civic matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Publicity is, in fact, one of the major functions of the Health Department, inasmuch as its constructive work depends to a considerable extent upon the public education it provides in combating evils...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design campaigns to inform behavior (e.g., disease prevention), combining facts with appeals that encourage cooperative public action; measure impact on knowledge and behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ PR for international recognition and nation-branding
rubrics_metrics.description: Lithuania... through the aid of a public relations expert, Lithuania issued pamphlets, it paraded, it figured in pictures and motion pictures and developed a favorable sentiment throughout the world...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use targeted international communications and cultural diplomacy to build recognition and sympathetic perceptions among foreign publics and governments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broaden campaign content beyond product to corporate conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The seller consider, for instance, in his sales campaign, not only the quality of his soap but the working conditions, the hours of labor, even the living conditions of the men who make it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight responsible practices—labor, safety, environmental stewardship—to influence public judgment and reduce vulnerabilities to criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be a student and researcher of the public mind
rubrics_metrics.description: The public relations counsel is first of all a student. His field of study is the public mind... He brings the talent of his intuitive understanding to the aid of his practical and psychological tests and surveys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop systematic observation, research skills, and continuous learning about social attitudes; combine intuition with empirical methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use research instruments: surveys, symposiums, and polls to gauge public opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: He employs the research campaign, the symposium, the survey of a particular group or of a particular state of mind as a further aid, and confirmation or modification of his own appraisals and judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validate strategic hypotheses with primary research; use surveys and forums to confirm or adjust PR tactics and messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ a wide range of communication media
rubrics_metrics.description: He employs the research campaign... advertising, motion pictures, circular letters, booklets, handbills, speeches, meetings, parades, news articles, magazine articles and whatever other mediums there are through which public attention is reached and influenced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select channels appropriate to target audiences and messages; integrate mass media, print, events, and novel formats for maximum reach and effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate sensitivity to subtle and informal channels of public sentiment
rubrics_metrics.description: He must advise modifications in policy in accordance with such changes in the public point of view... the events which are forming hour by hour, as reported in the words that are spoken on the street, in the smoking cars, in the school room...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor informal conversations, cultural expressions, gossip and entertainment patter as early indicators of shifting opinion; incorporate qualitative listening into intelligence systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advise clients on policy changes as well as messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: His primary function now is not to bring his clients by chance to the public’s attention... but to advise his clients how positive results can be accomplished in the field of public relations and to keep them from drifting inadvertently into unfortunate or harmful situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend substantive organizational or operational changes (policies, practices) when necessary to sustain or repair reputation rather than only adjusting communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value journalistic training and understanding of the 'average' public
rubrics_metrics.description: The competent public relations counsel has generally had some newspaper training and that the value of this training 'is a keen sense of the likes and dislikes of what we call the public--that is, the average of men and women.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hire or train PR staff with newsroom experience to improve news judgment, pitch framing, and sensitivity to media workflows and audience preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serve as pleader: interpret public to client and client to public
rubrics_metrics.description: The public relations counsel is the pleader to the public of a point of view. He acts in this capacity as a consultant both in interpreting the public to his client and in helping to interpret his client to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance advocacy for the client with honest translation of public concerns to decision-makers; aim to shape both policy and perception ethically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be constructive and socially responsible in PR practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The public relations consultant is ideally a constructive force in the community. The results of his work are often accelerated interest in matters of value and importance to the social, economic or political life of the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize initiatives that deliver tangible public benefits and reinforce civic values, not merely short-term reputation gains.
